# stage: # The single declared contract per stage type (design/architecture.md §1 move 1).
# Read by lib/owed.sh (owed), ferry.sh select (verdicts→next), ferry.sh compose
# (manifests). Columns are ';'-separated lists. Dynamic owed additions (impl/fix:
# spec commit-units resolved via the progress ledger) are marked @cu.
# session: cold|warm-author|warm-reviewer — the static freshness column
#   (design/architecture.md §7); self-check asserts precheck/postcheck round 1
#   cold. Rounds ≥2 of a review stage always use the .warm.md TEMPLATE (round
#   semantics, written to work identically in any session); only the SPAWN may
#   degrade to cold-fallback when no live held session exists.
# manifest entries are placeholder=path-pattern; ROLE_CARD expands per role.
# THE MANIFEST IS DERIVED FROM THE STAGE'S OWN CHECKLIST, and that is a rule
# rather than an observation: an artifact a stage's checklist names is an
# artifact its manifest owes. Measured — precheck's P7 checks the
# spec's citations against the PLAN and P8 audits "each decisions-surface entry
# of this slice", postcheck's C0 sweeps the same DP set against the precheck
# review, and none of the four was in either manifest. Every reviewer went and
# found them: 21 of 21 precheck rounds across two topics named a DP id and
# cited the plan, at 2.0 plan commands per session. So the cost was paid every
# round by the diligent, and the exposure was a less diligent one skipping a
# duty it was never handed the input for. When a checklist gains an item that
# names an artifact, this row owes the entry in the same commit.
# The rule's WORKFLOW-DOC half is now mechanical, not remembered: 30-closure
# asserts that any runtime-doc a stage's own prompt cites in backticks appears
# in that stage's manifest. Applied, it moved 8 stages' STANDARDS,
# 5 stages' PROTOCOL and close-out's OPERATIONS, all previously carried only as
# a prose citation next to a section number. The evidence that decided it is
# the FINGERPRINT, not a reading habit: compose_fingerprint hashes the content
# of every manifest-RESOLVED input, so `review-standards.md` was novelty for a
# precheck retry and invisible to a spec retry -- confirmed in the archived
# input sidecars, where precheck's lists review-standards.md and spec's does
# not, though both prompts bind their stage to it by section. An owner edit to
# the spec-ready contract could therefore land a `no_novelty` park on the very
# stage that contract governs. Zero new resolver code: _compose_resolve's first
# arm already accepted cards/*, review-standards.md, protocol.md and
# operations.md; nothing had ever asked it for the last two.
